findings.title: Unlimited fragment reassembly in receive_data may lead to resource exhaustion
findings.body: The receive_data method was changed to loop and reassemble COTP DT fragments until the EOT bit is set, whereas before it processed one TPKT frame per call. This change supports fragmentation but introduces a resource exhaustion risk: a client could send many fragments without setting EOT, causing unbounded memory growth. Additionally, the method does not validate that the COTP PDU length (from the TPKT header) matches the length of the received COTP PDU, which could lead to accepting malformed packets. Add a maximum fragment count or maximum reassembled size, and validate the COTP PDU length against the TPKT header length.

findings.title: Incorrect length field in _build_cotp_cc COTP PDU
findings.body: The _build_cotp_cc method was changed to include a TPDU size parameter in the COTP CC message, but the length field in the COTP PDU is set incorrectly. The method sets pdu_length to 6 + len(pdu_size_param) (9) but then builds a base PDU that is only 8 bytes (without the parameter) and appends the 3-byte parameter, resulting in an 11-byte COTP PDU. This inconsistency will cause the message to be parsed incorrectly by the peer. Fix the struct packing to correctly reflect the total length of the COTP PDU
